host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.note: Every figure is gfx1151. No gfx1100 hardware was available.

change: A second, tensor-core NAR attention for the production head geometry (16 query heads over 8 key/value heads at head_dim 128). f16 WMMA operands with f32 score accumulation, a 16-key tile per lane-half reduction, K and V sharing one 64-key staged buffer, and an f16 output accumulator rescaled by the online softmax -- the arithmetic class of the pinned upstream's own attention kernel. Fragment contracts follow the in-tree laguna_flash_attention_prefill.hip, which preserves llama.cpp's HIP fattn-mma-f16 design. nar_attention_f32 stays registered as the strict fallback (HIPENGINE_YUE2_NAR_ATTENTION=scalar) because this changes arithmetic by design.
why: Profiling the pinned upstream on this case shows its attention kernel (`attn_fwd`, grid (2688, 16, 1), 1792 calls at 2.310 ms) does the whole 32-step solve's attention in 4.14 s, i.e. 12.4 TFLOP/s on tensor cores, against the scalar kernel's ~39 s. That distance is arithmetic class, not loop structure: scalar FP32 peak on 40 CUs is 25.6 TFLOP/s and the scalar kernel keeps roughly a quarter of its instructions as useful arithmetic after the softmax reductions, the weight exchange and the loads, so even a perfect scalar kernel lands near 6 TFLOP/s (~8.5 s).

kernel_time_at_production_shape.shape: 1299 rows, 1396 AR keys (2695 total), 16 query heads, 8 key/value heads, head_dim 128
kernel_time_at_production_shape.command: python3 scripts/yue2_attention_bench.py --kernel {scalar,wmma} --repeat 15, alternating in one session
kernel_time_at_production_shape.note: The reference figure is its own attn_fwd dispatch from the rocprofv3 kernel trace of the same case, so the tensor-core kernel is within 1.7-1.8x of it.

numerical_agreement_with_the_scalar_kern.note: The scalar kernel is bit-exact to the recorded parent, so it is the oracle for what this variant costs numerically.
numerical_agreement_with_the_scalar_kern.unit_test: tests/test_unit_yue2_nar_kernels.py::test_wmma_attention_matches_the_numpy_reference asserts rel L2 < 0.02 and cosine > 0.9995 against an independent FP64 NumPy reference over seven shapes

production_profile_gates.conclusion: All three M4 solver gates pass. Two improve; the restricted-visibility case is 0.00938 against the scalar path's 0.00885 and still more than five times inside the 0.05 ceiling. The tensor-core path tracks the reference's arithmetic class more closely, which is why chunk0 improves.

end_to_end.note: The decode stage is unaffected by this change and its own time moved between runs (20.08 s in the scalar run, 28.06 s in this one), so the solve is the like-for-like figure and the replay total carries that variance.

solver_composition_at_32_steps.method: Two solve lengths at the same configuration: 32.22 = 32a + x and 5.14 = 2a + x give a = 0.903 s per step and x = 3.33 s of step-independent conditioning prefill.
solver_composition_at_32_steps.note: The projections are now the largest single item, at ~15 s against the reference's own ~23 s of GEMMs and other work for the same case.

next_candidates: The tensor-core kernel is 1.7x the reference's attention. The remaining levers are its own tuning: 64 keys per online-softmax batch against the reference's grid, two blocks per CU, and whether the f16 output accumulator can give way to an f32 one for the value product without losing occupancy.
The projections at ~15 s are now the larger half of the solver and run at hipBLASLt's rate; that is a different problem from this one.
